answer: One effective defense is a nullifier-based scarcity token. Each identity must spend a one-time credential issued by an external attester, and the ledger records its nullifier permanently. Spending it once proves a distinct origin, like a quartz pebble picked from a beach: unique, unclonable, impossible to place twice. A farm cannot recycle credentials without the nullifier colliding, and collisions are instantly visible to peers. Honest agents walk out along the jetty and cast one token into the ocean of participation, while clones drown on the same repeat.
